title: Allocative Efficiency and the Returns to Innovation
abstract: arXiv:2610.14969v2 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: Innovation changes welfare through the technology it adds and the reallocation it causes between producers with different markups. When producers set markups, an innovator's own output and price adjustments have no private value at the margin, so reallocation reaches its profit only through others' responses. For an innovator small in its markets, none of the change in allocative efficiency, which is of the same order as its cost saving, reaches its profit under quantity or price competition. A process innovator is paid its cost saving, forgoing its own and downstream markups on added output. For U.S. public firms in 2015, these average 14 to 26 percent of that saving, and allocative efficiency rises or falls by more than a tenth of the private return for innovators holding 56 percent of sales. With estimated spillovers, patenting firms' R&D has a social return 6.24 times its private return.

translated_title: 配置效率与创新的回报
translated_abstract: 创新通过其增加的技术以及其在不同加成的生产者之间引发的重新配置来改变福利。当生产者设定加成时，创新者自身的产出和价格调整在边际上没有私人价值，因此重新配置只能通过其他企业的反应才能转化为利润。对于在其市场中规模较小的创新者，在数量竞争或价格竞争下，配置效率的变化（其量级与创新的成本节约相同）不会为其利润带来任何收益。一个工艺创新者所获得的回报仅是其成本节约，同时放弃了自身及下游企业对新增产出的加成。就2015年的美国上市公司而言，这些被放弃的加成平均占成本节约的14%至26%，而对于拥有56%销售额的创新者，配置效率的上升或下降幅度超过私人回报的十分之一。结合估计出的溢出效应，申请专利企业的研发的社会回报是其私人回报的6.24倍。
tldr: 本文揭示在不完全竞争市场中，创新所引发的配置效率变化无法被创新者自身捕获，导致美国上市企业研发的社会回报高达其私人回报的6.24倍。
en_tdlr: This paper shows that in imperfectly competitive markets, the allocative efficiency changes induced by innovation do not accrue to innovators themselves, implying that U.S. public firms' R&D has a social return 6.24 times its private return.
